newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - St George /Advance on S&P creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - St George /Advance on S&P creditwatch.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Monday that it placed the long and short-term counterparty ratings of St George Bank Ltd on creditwatch with positive implications.
The ratings agency also said it placed the long and short-term counterparty ratings of Advance Bank Australia Ltd on creditwatch with negative implications.
St George, which earlier on Monday announced the A$2.65 billion friendly takeover of Advance, has an A minus long term and an A2 short term counterparty rating.
Advance has an A long term and an A1 short term counterparty rating.

S&P said it also placed St George's A minus floating rate note, BBB plus subordinated debt issue ratings, and A2 certificates of deposit ratings of St George on creditwatch with positive implications.

S&P said Advance's A minus floating rate note and A minus subordinated note issue ratings had been placed on creditwatch with negative implications as had the A1 rating on its certificates of deposits, as well as the A long term and A1 short term ratings of the Advance unit Bank of South Australia.
It said the takeover should greatly enhance St George's credit profile, effectively doubling its total asset size and making it four times larger than the next largest regional bank.

"The CreditWatch with negative implications on Advance reflects the possibility that the credit risk associated with the debt obligations of Advance, which will be acquired by St George, could remain the same or, alternatively, be lowered, should Standard and Poor's view that the credit profile and the risks of the merger of the two banks reflects more accurately a rating at a lower level," S&P said.
It said the acquisition of Advance would provide St George management with a number of challenges, including the rationalisation of the branch networks in which there existed considerable overlap.
